features: The phone number is the biggest thing on the first screen, and it switches between the office and the emergency mobile on the clock, so night callers ring someone who answers
Every service is a breaker on a consumer unit: switch one on to see what is included, what it costs and who does it
Prices on the page, fixed before the work starts, so the call starts with a yes
A postcode check, a written-quote form and a Call and Quote bar that stays on screen on a phone
name: Kestrel Electrical
short: An electrician's site where every job is a breaker you can switch on.
long: A photo-led first screen with the number at poster size and a 24-hour line that answers. Below it, the services are a real consumer unit: switch a breaker on and it shows what is included, the price and a button to ring. Then the price list, a review over a real job, the emergency line, a postcode check and a written-quote form.
proves: Someone with the power off can ring the right number in one tap, at any hour, and know the price before they do.
story: Most trade sites bury the number under a slogan and a form nobody fills in. This one leads with the number and the work, and borrows the thing an electrician opens every day: the board. Every job is a switch, and the main switch rings the phone.
